newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy inflation slows to lowest rate for 28 years.
newsitem.headline: Italy inflation slows to lowest rate for 28 years.

text.p: Italian inflation slowed to its lowest level in 28 years in April, fuelling speculation in financial markets that the Bank of Italy may move to lower official interest rates soon.

Figures released Tuesday by the government statistics institute Istat showed consumer price increases slowed to a 1.7 percent annual rate last month, compared with 2.2 percent in March. It was the tamest rate of growth since April 1969.
Italian bonds and futures climbed after the news, which investors saw as increasing chances the Bank of Italy could lower the official discount rate in the near future.
The discount rate, which stands at 6.75 percent, was last lowered in January.
